# Booking a Flight Reservation

The `book_reservation` tool creates a new flight reservation for a user. It requires collecting trip details, passenger information, cabin class, baggage counts, insurance preference, and payment methods before calling the API.

## Key Points

- Call `book_reservation` with `user_id`, `origin`, `destination`, `flight_type` (`one_way` or `round_trip`), `cabin`, `flights` (array of flight number + date objects), `passengers` (array with `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`), `payment_methods` (array of payment id + amount objects), `total_baggages`, `nonfree_baggages`, and `insurance` (`yes`/`no`) [1]
- The passenger's date of birth can be retrieved from the user profile (via `get_user_details`) if the passenger is the booking user — no need to ask the user to re-enter it [1]
- Compute `nonfree_baggages` as the number of checked bags exceeding the free allowance for the user's membership level and cabin class; each extra bag costs $50. The API does NOT compute this automatically — the agent must calculate it [1]
- The free checked bag allowance for Gold members in economy is 3 bags per passenger; always retrieve the user's membership level before quoting baggage costs [1]
- The `book_reservation` API does NOT enforce the policy limit of at most one travel certificate per reservation — the agent must verify this constraint before calling the API [1]
- Always confirm full booking details with the user (flights, passenger info, cabin, baggage count, payment breakdown, insurance) and receive explicit confirmation before calling `book_reservation` [1]
- When a user wants to apply multiple travel certificates (one per passenger), a multi-passenger itinerary can be split into separate single-passenger reservations — each reservation accepts one certificate. All separate reservations must use the same flights and cabin class. The `book_reservation` API accepts single-passenger reservations without restriction [5]
- NEVER submit payment method amounts that sum to more (or less) than the total reservation price — the API enforces exact payment matching and returns an error if the amounts do not add up. Correct action: calculate the exact total price first, then allocate payment amounts so they sum precisely to that total (e.g., split across certificates/cards as needed). SCOPE: constructing the `payment_methods` array in `book_reservation` [5]

- prerequisite [[concepts/searching-onestop-flights.md]] — search for one-stop options when direct flights are unavailable or don't meet user constraints

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Locating a Reservation by Flight Details

When a user does not know their reservation ID but can describe the flight (origin, destination, date, etc.), the agent must retrieve the user's profile to obtain all reservation IDs, then call `get_reservation_details` on each one until the matching reservation is found.

## Key Points

- Retrieve the user profile via `get_user_details` first; the profile contains the list of all reservation IDs associated with that user [1]
- Iterate through each reservation ID by calling `get_reservation_details` one at a time until the reservation matching the user's described flight (origin, destination, date, cabin, etc.) is identified [1]
- Each reservation must be evaluated independently for cancellation or modification eligibility — a reservation that is ineligible does not affect eligibility assessment of another reservation for the same user [1]
- When a user asks to cancel a specific ineligible flight and then requests cancellation of an alternative flight instead, re-assess eligibility from scratch for the new reservation before proceeding [1]

# Booking a Flight Reservation

The `book_reservation` tool creates a new flight reservation for a user. It requires collecting trip details, passenger information, cabin class, baggage counts, insurance preference, and payment methods before calling the API.

## Key Points

- Call `book_reservation` with `user_id`, `origin`, `destination`, `flight_type` (`one_way` or `round_trip`), `cabin`, `flights` (array of flight number + date objects), `passengers` (array with `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`), `payment_methods` (array of payment id + amount objects), `total_baggages`, `nonfree_baggages`, and `insurance` (`yes`/`no`) [1]
- The passenger's date of birth can be retrieved from the user profile (via `get_user_details`) if the passenger is the booking user — no need to ask the user to re-enter it [1]
- Compute `nonfree_baggages` as the number of checked bags exceeding the free allowance for the user's membership level and cabin class; each extra bag costs $50. The API does NOT compute this automatically — the agent must calculate it [1]
- The free checked bag allowance for Gold members in economy is 3 bags per passenger; always retrieve the user's membership level before quoting baggage costs [1]
- The `book_reservation` API does NOT enforce the policy limit of at most one travel certificate per reservation — the agent must verify this constraint before calling the API [1]
- Always confirm full booking details with the user (flights, passenger info, cabin, baggage count, payment breakdown, insurance) and receive explicit confirmation before calling `book_reservation` [1]
- When a user wants to apply multiple travel certificates (one per passenger), a multi-passenger itinerary can be split into separate single-passenger reservations — each reservation accepts one certificate. All separate reservations must use the same flights and cabin class. The `book_reservation` API accepts single-passenger reservations without restriction [5]
- NEVER submit payment method amounts that sum to more (or less) than the total reservation price — the API enforces exact payment matching and returns an error if the amounts do not add up. Correct action: calculate the exact total price first, then allocate payment amounts so they sum precisely to that total (e.g., split across certificates/cards as needed). SCOPE: constructing the `payment_methods` array in `book_reservation` [5]

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Searching for Flights

Two tools are available for finding flights between airports on a given date: `search_direct_flight` for nonstop itineraries and `search_onestop_flight` for connecting itineraries. Both accept the same core parameters and return an empty array when no flights are available. The standard pattern is to search direct flights first, then fall back to one-stop options when direct flights are unavailable or don't satisfy the user's constraints.

## Key Points

- Call `search_direct_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available nonstop flights on a route [1]
- Call `search_onestop_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available one-stop (connecting) itineraries on a route [5]
- Both tools return an empty array `[]` when no flights are available for the requested route and date — treat this as a definitive 'no availability' result and inform the user accordingly [1][5]
- One-stop results are returned as arrays of flight pairs (two-segment itineraries); each segment has its own flight number, departure/arrival times, and pricing [5]
- Default search order: try direct flights first; fall back to one-stop search when direct flights are unavailable or don't meet user constraints (e.g., departure time preferences) [5][9]
- When the user accepts any NYC-area airport, search all relevant origin airports (e.g., JFK, LGA, EWR) separately for both direct and one-stop options to surface the best availability [5]

## Direct Flight Search

Use `search_direct_flight` when you need to verify nonstop availability or when a user explicitly requests a direct flight. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date` (departure date). If the result is an empty array, there are no nonstop options for that route and date, and the user should be informed [1][2][3].

## One-Stop Flight Search

Use `search_onestop_flight` when direct flights are unavailable, when the user's schedule constraints rule out available nonstop options, or when the user explicitly wants to explore connecting flights. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date`. Results are arrays of two-segment itinerary pairs, each with flight number, times, and price. An empty array means no one-stop options exist for the route and date [4][5][11][12].

## Search Strategy and Fallback Logic

The recommended workflow is to search for direct flights first. If `search_direct_flight` returns an empty array or no suitable options, proceed with `search_onestop_flight` as a fallback. Present the available alternatives to the user rather than stopping at the first 'no availability' result [5][9].

## Multi-Airport Markets

When a user indicates flexibility around a major metro area with multiple airports (e.g., New York City: JFK, LGA, EWR), run separate searches for each airport code for both direct and one-stop options. This ensures the broadest possible availability is surfaced before concluding that no flights exist [5].

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Booking a Flight Reservation

The `book_reservation` tool creates a new flight reservation for a user. It requires collecting trip details, passenger information, cabin class, baggage counts, insurance preference, and payment methods before calling the API.

## Key Points

- Call `book_reservation` with `user_id`, `origin`, `destination`, `flight_type` (`one_way` or `round_trip`), `cabin`, `flights` (array of flight number + date objects), `passengers` (array with `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`), `payment_methods` (array of payment id + amount objects), `total_baggages`, `nonfree_baggages`, and `insurance` (`yes`/`no`) [1]
- The passenger's date of birth can be retrieved from the user profile (via `get_user_details`) if the passenger is the booking user — no need to ask the user to re-enter it [1]
- Compute `nonfree_baggages` as the number of checked bags exceeding the free allowance for the user's membership level and cabin class; each extra bag costs $50. The API does NOT compute this automatically — the agent must calculate it [1]
- The free checked bag allowance for Gold members in economy is 3 bags per passenger; always retrieve the user's membership level before quoting baggage costs [1]
- The `book_reservation` API does NOT enforce the policy limit of at most one travel certificate per reservation — the agent must verify this constraint before calling the API [1]

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

# Booking a Flight Reservation

The `book_reservation` tool creates a new flight reservation for a user. It requires collecting trip details, passenger information, cabin class, baggage counts, insurance preference, and payment methods before calling the API.

## Key Points

- Call `book_reservation` with `user_id`, `origin`, `destination`, `flight_type` (`one_way` or `round_trip`), `cabin`, `flights` (array of flight number + date objects), `passengers` (array with `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`), `payment_methods` (array of payment id + amount objects), `total_baggages`, `nonfree_baggages`, and `insurance` (`yes`/`no`) [1]
- The passenger's date of birth can be retrieved from the user profile (via `get_user_details`) if the passenger is the booking user — no need to ask the user to re-enter it [1]
- Compute `nonfree_baggages` as the number of checked bags exceeding the free allowance for the user's membership level and cabin class; each extra bag costs $50. The API does NOT compute this automatically — the agent must calculate it [1]
- The free checked bag allowance for Gold members in economy is 3 bags per passenger; always retrieve the user's membership level before quoting baggage costs [1]
- The `book_reservation` API does NOT enforce the policy limit of at most one travel certificate per reservation — the agent must verify this constraint before calling the API [1]
- Always confirm full booking details with the user (flights, passenger info, cabin, baggage count, payment breakdown, insurance) and receive explicit confirmation before calling `book_reservation` [1]
- When a user wants to apply multiple travel certificates (one per passenger), a multi-passenger itinerary can be split into separate single-passenger reservations — each reservation accepts one certificate. All separate reservations must use the same flights and cabin class. The `book_reservation` API accepts single-passenger reservations without restriction [5]
- NEVER submit payment method amounts that sum to more (or less) than the total reservation price — the API enforces exact payment matching and returns an error if the amounts do not add up. Correct action: calculate the exact total price first, then allocate payment amounts so they sum precisely to that total (e.g., split across certificates/cards as needed). SCOPE: constructing the `payment_methods` array in `book_reservation` [5]

# Searching for Flights

Two tools are available for finding flights between airports on a given date: `search_direct_flight` for nonstop itineraries and `search_onestop_flight` for connecting itineraries. Both accept the same core parameters and return an empty array when no flights are available. The standard pattern is to search direct flights first, then fall back to one-stop options when direct flights are unavailable or don't satisfy the user's constraints.

## Key Points

- Call `search_direct_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available nonstop flights on a route [1]
- Call `search_onestop_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available one-stop (connecting) itineraries on a route [5]
- Both tools return an empty array `[]` when no flights are available for the requested route and date — treat this as a definitive 'no availability' result and inform the user accordingly [1][5]
- One-stop results are returned as arrays of flight pairs (two-segment itineraries); each segment has its own flight number, departure/arrival times, and pricing [5]
- Default search order: try direct flights first; fall back to one-stop search when direct flights are unavailable or don't meet user constraints (e.g., departure time preferences) [5][9]
- When the user accepts any NYC-area airport, search all relevant origin airports (e.g., JFK, LGA, EWR) separately for both direct and one-stop options to surface the best availability [5]

## Direct Flight Search

Use `search_direct_flight` when you need to verify nonstop availability or when a user explicitly requests a direct flight. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date` (departure date). If the result is an empty array, there are no nonstop options for that route and date, and the user should be informed [1][2][3].

## One-Stop Flight Search

Use `search_onestop_flight` when direct flights are unavailable, when the user's schedule constraints rule out available nonstop options, or when the user explicitly wants to explore connecting flights. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date`. Results are arrays of two-segment itinerary pairs, each with flight number, times, and price. An empty array means no one-stop options exist for the route and date [4][5][11][12].

## Search Strategy and Fallback Logic

The recommended workflow is to search for direct flights first. If `search_direct_flight` returns an empty array or no suitable options, proceed with `search_onestop_flight` as a fallback. Present the available alternatives to the user rather than stopping at the first 'no availability' result [5][9].

## Multi-Airport Markets

When a user indicates flexibility around a major metro area with multiple airports (e.g., New York City: JFK, LGA, EWR), run separate searches for each airport code for both direct and one-stop options. This ensures the broadest possible availability is surfaced before concluding that no flights exist [5].

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Cancelling a Basic Economy Reservation via Cabin Upgrade

Basic economy reservations cannot normally be cancelled unless specific conditions apply (e.g., within 24 hrs of booking, airline cancellation). However, because cabin changes are permitted on all reservation types including basic economy, upgrading to business class first enables cancellation under the business class rule.

## Key Points

- Although basic economy flight segments cannot be modified (no flight changes), the cabin class CAN be changed on a basic economy reservation — this rule applies to all reservation types [1]
- After a cabin upgrade from basic economy to business, the reservation qualifies as a business reservation and can be cancelled under the business-class cancellation rule [1]
- The `update_reservation_flights` API accepts cabin-only changes (no flight number or date changes) for basic economy reservations without error — the upgrade from basic economy to business was confirmed as successful [1]
- The upgrade-then-cancel sequence requires two separate API calls: first `update_reservation_flights` (with the same flights but new cabin), then `cancel_reservation` [1]
- When changing cabin class on a reservation, if the new cabin price is higher the user must pay the difference; a payment method already in the user profile is required for this step [1]

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Searching for Flights

Two tools are available for finding flights between airports on a given date: `search_direct_flight` for nonstop itineraries and `search_onestop_flight` for connecting itineraries. Both accept the same core parameters and return an empty array when no flights are available. The standard pattern is to search direct flights first, then fall back to one-stop options when direct flights are unavailable or don't satisfy the user's constraints.

## Key Points

- Call `search_direct_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available nonstop flights on a route [1]
- Call `search_onestop_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available one-stop (connecting) itineraries on a route [5]
- Both tools return an empty array `[]` when no flights are available for the requested route and date — treat this as a definitive 'no availability' result and inform the user accordingly [1][5]
- One-stop results are returned as arrays of flight pairs (two-segment itineraries); each segment has its own flight number, departure/arrival times, and pricing [5]
- Default search order: try direct flights first; fall back to one-stop search when direct flights are unavailable or don't meet user constraints (e.g., departure time preferences) [5][9]
- When the user accepts any NYC-area airport, search all relevant origin airports (e.g., JFK, LGA, EWR) separately for both direct and one-stop options to surface the best availability [5]

## Direct Flight Search

Use `search_direct_flight` when you need to verify nonstop availability or when a user explicitly requests a direct flight. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date` (departure date). If the result is an empty array, there are no nonstop options for that route and date, and the user should be informed [1][2][3].

## One-Stop Flight Search

Use `search_onestop_flight` when direct flights are unavailable, when the user's schedule constraints rule out available nonstop options, or when the user explicitly wants to explore connecting flights. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date`. Results are arrays of two-segment itinerary pairs, each with flight number, times, and price. An empty array means no one-stop options exist for the route and date [4][5][11][12].

## Search Strategy and Fallback Logic

The recommended workflow is to search for direct flights first. If `search_direct_flight` returns an empty array or no suitable options, proceed with `search_onestop_flight` as a fallback. Present the available alternatives to the user rather than stopping at the first 'no availability' result [5][9].

## Multi-Airport Markets

When a user indicates flexibility around a major metro area with multiple airports (e.g., New York City: JFK, LGA, EWR), run separate searches for each airport code for both direct and one-stop options. This ensures the broadest possible availability is surfaced before concluding that no flights exist [5].

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Searching for Flights

Two tools are available for finding flights between airports on a given date: `search_direct_flight` for nonstop itineraries and `search_onestop_flight` for connecting itineraries. Both accept the same core parameters and return an empty array when no flights are available. The standard pattern is to search direct flights first, then fall back to one-stop options when direct flights are unavailable or don't satisfy the user's constraints.

## Key Points

- Call `search_direct_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available nonstop flights on a route [1]
- Call `search_onestop_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available one-stop (connecting) itineraries on a route [5]
- Both tools return an empty array `[]` when no flights are available for the requested route and date — treat this as a definitive 'no availability' result and inform the user accordingly [1][5]
- One-stop results are returned as arrays of flight pairs (two-segment itineraries); each segment has its own flight number, departure/arrival times, and pricing [5]
- Default search order: try direct flights first; fall back to one-stop search when direct flights are unavailable or don't meet user constraints (e.g., departure time preferences) [5][9]
- When the user accepts any NYC-area airport, search all relevant origin airports (e.g., JFK, LGA, EWR) separately for both direct and one-stop options to surface the best availability [5]

## Direct Flight Search

Use `search_direct_flight` when you need to verify nonstop availability or when a user explicitly requests a direct flight. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date` (departure date). If the result is an empty array, there are no nonstop options for that route and date, and the user should be informed [1][2][3].

## One-Stop Flight Search

Use `search_onestop_flight` when direct flights are unavailable, when the user's schedule constraints rule out available nonstop options, or when the user explicitly wants to explore connecting flights. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date`. Results are arrays of two-segment itinerary pairs, each with flight number, times, and price. An empty array means no one-stop options exist for the route and date [4][5][11][12].

## Search Strategy and Fallback Logic

The recommended workflow is to search for direct flights first. If `search_direct_flight` returns an empty array or no suitable options, proceed with `search_onestop_flight` as a fallback. Present the available alternatives to the user rather than stopping at the first 'no availability' result [5][9].

## Multi-Airport Markets

When a user indicates flexibility around a major metro area with multiple airports (e.g., New York City: JFK, LGA, EWR), run separate searches for each airport code for both direct and one-stop options. This ensures the broadest possible availability is surfaced before concluding that no flights exist [5].

# Locating a Reservation by Flight Details

When a user does not know their reservation ID but can describe the flight (origin, destination, date, etc.), the agent must retrieve the user's profile to obtain all reservation IDs, then call `get_reservation_details` on each one until the matching reservation is found.

## Key Points

- Retrieve the user profile via `get_user_details` first; the profile contains the list of all reservation IDs associated with that user [1]
- Iterate through each reservation ID by calling `get_reservation_details` one at a time until the reservation matching the user's described flight (origin, destination, date, cabin, etc.) is identified [1]
- Each reservation must be evaluated independently for cancellation or modification eligibility — a reservation that is ineligible does not affect eligibility assessment of another reservation for the same user [1]
- When a user asks to cancel a specific ineligible flight and then requests cancellation of an alternative flight instead, re-assess eligibility from scratch for the new reservation before proceeding [1]

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Locating a Reservation by Flight Details

When a user does not know their reservation ID but can describe the flight (origin, destination, date, etc.), the agent must retrieve the user's profile to obtain all reservation IDs, then call `get_reservation_details` on each one until the matching reservation is found.

## Key Points

- Retrieve the user profile via `get_user_details` first; the profile contains the list of all reservation IDs associated with that user [1]
- Iterate through each reservation ID by calling `get_reservation_details` one at a time until the reservation matching the user's described flight (origin, destination, date, cabin, etc.) is identified [1]
- Each reservation must be evaluated independently for cancellation or modification eligibility — a reservation that is ineligible does not affect eligibility assessment of another reservation for the same user [1]
- When a user asks to cancel a specific ineligible flight and then requests cancellation of an alternative flight instead, re-assess eligibility from scratch for the new reservation before proceeding [1]

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Updating Reservation Baggages

The `update_reservation_baggages` tool adds checked bags to an existing reservation. It requires specifying both the total bag count and the number of non-free (paid) bags, which depends on the passenger's membership level and cabin class.

## Key Points

- Call `update_reservation_baggages` with `reservation_id`, `total_baggages`, `nonfree_baggages`, and `payment_id` to add checked bags to a reservation [1]
- The `nonfree_baggages` value must be computed from the free bag allowance: subtract the free bags (determined by membership level × cabin class) from `total_baggages`; only the excess is charged at $50 each [1]
- Free bag allowances by membership and cabin: regular gets 0/1/2 free bags for basic economy/economy/business; silver gets 1/2/3; gold gets 2/3/4 — apply these before setting `nonfree_baggages` [1]
- The user can add bags but cannot remove them — `total_baggages` must be greater than or equal to the current bag count on the reservation [1]
- A `payment_id` is required even when `nonfree_baggages` is 0 (all bags are free) — always include a valid gift card or credit card from the user's profile [1]

## Related Concepts

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Booking a Flight Reservation

The `book_reservation` tool creates a new flight reservation for a user. It requires collecting trip details, passenger information, cabin class, baggage counts, insurance preference, and payment methods before calling the API.

## Key Points

- Call `book_reservation` with `user_id`, `origin`, `destination`, `flight_type` (`one_way` or `round_trip`), `cabin`, `flights` (array of flight number + date objects), `passengers` (array with `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`), `payment_methods` (array of payment id + amount objects), `total_baggages`, `nonfree_baggages`, and `insurance` (`yes`/`no`) [1]
- The passenger's date of birth can be retrieved from the user profile (via `get_user_details`) if the passenger is the booking user — no need to ask the user to re-enter it [1]
- Compute `nonfree_baggages` as the number of checked bags exceeding the free allowance for the user's membership level and cabin class; each extra bag costs $50. The API does NOT compute this automatically — the agent must calculate it [1]
- The free checked bag allowance for Gold members in economy is 3 bags per passenger; always retrieve the user's membership level before quoting baggage costs [1]
- The `book_reservation` API does NOT enforce the policy limit of at most one travel certificate per reservation — the agent must verify this constraint before calling the API [1]
- Always confirm full booking details with the user (flights, passenger info, cabin, baggage count, payment breakdown, insurance) and receive explicit confirmation before calling `book_reservation` [1]
- When a user wants to apply multiple travel certificates (one per passenger), a multi-passenger itinerary can be split into separate single-passenger reservations — each reservation accepts one certificate. All separate reservations must use the same flights and cabin class. The `book_reservation` API accepts single-passenger reservations without restriction [5]
- NEVER submit payment method amounts that sum to more (or less) than the total reservation price — the API enforces exact payment matching and returns an error if the amounts do not add up. Correct action: calculate the exact total price first, then allocate payment amounts so they sum precisely to that total (e.g., split across certificates/cards as needed). SCOPE: constructing the `payment_methods` array in `book_reservation` [5]

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Cancellation Eligibility Check

Before cancelling any reservation, the agent must manually verify that at least one cancellation condition is satisfied. The `cancel_reservation` API does not enforce eligibility rules — it will accept and execute a cancellation even when none of the conditions are met.

## Key Points

- The `cancel_reservation` API does NOT check cancellation eligibility — it will succeed even for ineligible reservations. The agent must verify eligibility before calling the API [1]
- A reservation is eligible for cancellation only if at least one of the following is true: (a) booking was made within the last 24 hours, (b) the airline cancelled the flight, (c) it is a business class reservation, or (d) the user has travel insurance and the cancellation reason is covered (health or weather) [1]
- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]
- If any portion of the flight has already been flown, cancellation is not possible even if other conditions are met — transfer to a human agent is required in that case [1]
- The refund goes to the original payment method(s) within 5–7 business days [1]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/cancelling-basic-economy-via-cabin-upgrade.md]] — workaround for cancelling a basic economy reservation that would otherwise not qualify

- NEVER call `cancel_reservation` for a basic economy reservation booked more than 24 hours ago with a 'change of plan' reason and no travel insurance — none of the eligibility conditions are met. Correct action: inform the user the reservation does not qualify for cancellation. SCOPE: basic economy reservations with change-of-plan reason [1]

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Updating Reservation Flights

The `update_reservation_flights` tool modifies the flights and/or cabin class in an existing reservation. It requires a payment method to cover any fare difference or process any refund.

## Key Points

- NEVER pass a travel certificate as the `payment_id` to `update_reservation_flights` — the API explicitly rejects it with `'Certificate cannot be used to update reservation'`. Correct action: use a gift card or credit card from the user's profile instead. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [4]
- The `payment_id` must reference a gift card or credit card already in the user's profile; verify the card has sufficient balance before calling, as the API returns `'Gift card balance is not enough'` otherwise [4]
- Cabin class must be the same for all flights submitted in a single `update_reservation_flights` call — the API applies the specified `cabin` uniformly across all flight segments [4]
- A flight returned by `search_onestop_flight` (or `search_direct_flight`) as 'available' may still cause `update_reservation_flights` to fail with `'Not enough seats on flight <X>'` — availability in search results does not guarantee seats at update time. Correct action: retry with the next available flight option from the search results. SCOPE: changing flights in a reservation [6]
- Cabin class can be changed to `basic_economy` on a business reservation (downgrade) even when the original cabin was business — the `update_reservation_flights` tool accepts a lower cabin class, and the fare difference is refunded to the specified payment method [7]

## Related Concepts

- related [[concepts/searching-direct-flights.md]] — search for available direct flight options before calling update_reservation_flights

# Searching for Flights

Two tools are available for finding flights between airports on a given date: `search_direct_flight` for nonstop itineraries and `search_onestop_flight` for connecting itineraries. Both accept the same core parameters and return an empty array when no flights are available. The standard pattern is to search direct flights first, then fall back to one-stop options when direct flights are unavailable or don't satisfy the user's constraints.

## Key Points

- Call `search_direct_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available nonstop flights on a route [1]
- Call `search_onestop_flight` with `origin`, `destination`, and `date` to retrieve available one-stop (connecting) itineraries on a route [5]
- Both tools return an empty array `[]` when no flights are available for the requested route and date — treat this as a definitive 'no availability' result and inform the user accordingly [1][5]
- One-stop results are returned as arrays of flight pairs (two-segment itineraries); each segment has its own flight number, departure/arrival times, and pricing [5]
- Default search order: try direct flights first; fall back to one-stop search when direct flights are unavailable or don't meet user constraints (e.g., departure time preferences) [5][9]
- When the user accepts any NYC-area airport, search all relevant origin airports (e.g., JFK, LGA, EWR) separately for both direct and one-stop options to surface the best availability [5]

## Direct Flight Search

Use `search_direct_flight` when you need to verify nonstop availability or when a user explicitly requests a direct flight. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date` (departure date). If the result is an empty array, there are no nonstop options for that route and date, and the user should be informed [1][2][3].

## One-Stop Flight Search

Use `search_onestop_flight` when direct flights are unavailable, when the user's schedule constraints rule out available nonstop options, or when the user explicitly wants to explore connecting flights. Pass `origin`, `destination`, and `date`. Results are arrays of two-segment itinerary pairs, each with flight number, times, and price. An empty array means no one-stop options exist for the route and date [4][5][11][12].

## Search Strategy and Fallback Logic

The recommended workflow is to search for direct flights first. If `search_direct_flight` returns an empty array or no suitable options, proceed with `search_onestop_flight` as a fallback. Present the available alternatives to the user rather than stopping at the first 'no availability' result [5][9].

## Multi-Airport Markets

When a user indicates flexibility around a major metro area with multiple airports (e.g., New York City: JFK, LGA, EWR), run separate searches for each airport code for both direct and one-stop options. This ensures the broadest possible availability is surfaced before concluding that no flights exist [5].

# Locating a Reservation by Flight Details

When a user does not know their reservation ID but can describe the flight (origin, destination, date, etc.), the agent must retrieve the user's profile to obtain all reservation IDs, then call `get_reservation_details` on each one until the matching reservation is found.

## Key Points

- Retrieve the user profile via `get_user_details` first; the profile contains the list of all reservation IDs associated with that user [1]
- Iterate through each reservation ID by calling `get_reservation_details` one at a time until the reservation matching the user's described flight (origin, destination, date, cabin, etc.) is identified [1]
- Each reservation must be evaluated independently for cancellation or modification eligibility — a reservation that is ineligible does not affect eligibility assessment of another reservation for the same user [1]

# Delayed Flight Compensation

When a user complains about a delayed flight and wants to change or cancel their reservation, the agent may offer a travel certificate as a gesture of compensation. Compensation eligibility depends on membership level, cabin class, or travel insurance — not solely on the user's self-reported status.

## Key Points

- Compensation for a delayed flight is only available if the user is a silver/gold member, has travel insurance, or flies business class — regular members flying basic economy or economy without travel insurance are not eligible 
- Always verify the user's actual profile (via `get_user_details`) to confirm membership level — do not accept the user's self-reported membership level as authoritative 
- Always confirm the flight is actually delayed by calling `get_flight_status` before offering any compensation 
- Always locate the relevant reservation (via `get_reservation_details`) and confirm the cabin class and passenger count before calculating compensation 
- The compensation amount for a delayed flight is $50 times the number of passengers in the affected reservation 
- Compensation for delayed flights is only offered if the user wants to change or cancel the reservation — do not proactively offer it otherwise 
- Issue compensation by calling `send_certificate` with `user_id` and `amount`; the tool returns a certificate ID that should be communicated to the user 
- NEVER offer compensation for a delayed flight without first confirming the user wants to change or cancel the reservation, confirming the delay, and verifying eligibility. Correct action: follow the confirm-facts → verify-eligibility → offer-certificate sequence. SCOPE: delayed flight compensation 
- If `get_flight_status` returns an ambiguous status (e.g., `available`) for the claimed delayed flight rather than `delayed`, the delay cannot be confirmed from the tool alone — do not issue compensation based solely on the user's claim when the tool does not corroborate it 

## Related Concepts

- prerequisite [[concepts/locating-reservation-by-flight-details.md]] — locate the reservation to confirm cabin class and passenger count before calculating compensation

# Booking a Flight Reservation

The `book_reservation` tool creates a new flight reservation for a user. It requires collecting trip details, passenger information, cabin class, baggage counts, insurance preference, and payment methods before calling the API.

## Key Points

- Call `book_reservation` with `user_id`, `origin`, `destination`, `flight_type` (`one_way` or `round_trip`), `cabin`, `flights` (array of flight number + date objects), `passengers` (array with `first_name`, `last_name`, `dob`), `payment_methods` (array of payment id + amount objects), `total_baggages`, `nonfree_baggages`, and `insurance` (`yes`/`no`) [1]
- The passenger's date of birth can be retrieved from the user profile (via `get_user_details`) if the passenger is the booking user — no need to ask the user to re-enter it [1]
- Compute `nonfree_baggages` as the number of checked bags exceeding the free allowance for the user's membership level and cabin class; each extra bag costs $50. The API does NOT compute this automatically — the agent must calculate it [1]
- The free checked bag allowance for Gold members in economy is 3 bags per passenger; always retrieve the user's membership level before quoting baggage costs [1]
- The `book_reservation` API does NOT enforce the policy limit of at most one travel certificate per reservation — the agent must verify this constraint before calling the API [1]
- Always confirm full booking details with the user (flights, passenger info, cabin, baggage count, payment breakdown, insurance) and receive explicit confirmation before calling `book_reservation` [1]
- When a user wants to apply multiple travel certificates (one per passenger), a multi-passenger itinerary can be split into separate single-passenger reservations — each reservation accepts one certificate. All separate reservations must use the same flights and cabin class. The `book_reservation` API accepts single-passenger reservations without restriction [5]
- NEVER submit payment method amounts that sum to more (or less) than the total reservation price — the API enforces exact payment matching and returns an error if the amounts do not add up. Correct action: calculate the exact total price first, then allocate payment amounts so they sum precisely to that total (e.g., split across certificates/cards as needed). SCOPE: constructing the `payment_methods` array in `book_reservation` [5]
